paragraphs: Blackpool Council runs its own fostering service, and the independent agencies listed below also approve carers in the town. The council says it needs a diverse range of foster carers from all walks of life, including single people, couples, families with or without children, LGBT carers and people whose own children have left home.
It offers short breaks, emergency, long-term and mother and child fostering. To apply you need to be over 21 and have a spare bedroom; childcare experience is preferred but not required.

Council carers receive allowances meant to cover the full cost of caring for a child, with a payment for skills scheme that the team explains when you enquire. Each family has a supervising social worker, there is a 24-hour telephone duty service, and the council can provide equipment such as beds, car seats and stair gates. Training includes support to gain qualifications such as a Level 3 in health and social care, and there are support groups, coffee mornings, peer mentors for new carers and quarterly carer forums with managers.

In April 2026 the council was accredited as a Fostering Friendly employer by The Fostering Network: its own staff who foster, or are applying to, can take up to ten extra days of paid leave a year for training, panels, reviews and meetings, whichever fostering service they are with.
You can request an information pack or call the team on 01253 420222. Speak to two or three of the services on this page before you decide.
